findings.finding: Useful sagittal anatomy source; labels require full-resolution cross-check; source artwork not selected for automatic reuse.
Generic spherical gastrula would misrepresent human disc morphology if used without organism-specific qualification; replace core visual with human-specific original.
Generic spherical invagination and endoderm table overgeneralize organ origins; replace with human-disc view and tissue-specific destinations.
Video thumbnail visually associates X shape with diploid and single rod with haploid; do not reuse as a ploidy diagram. Chromosome sets and DNA-copy state need separate depiction.
Reduction label must refer to each segregated pole/resulting daughter cell, not treat the undivided anaphase-I cell as a completed haploid daughter.
Meiosis recap appears to label the two products of meiosis I as diploid. Full-resolution inspection required to pin the erroneous label; new teaching already uses n,2C after meiosis I.
A midpoint map is presented from only H–N 25 and E–N 12.5; E could be on either side of N without H–E evidence. Preserve ambiguity in an original map problem.
Rendered source table confirms incompatible coding-strand, RNA and amino-acid claims. Rewrite one explicit strand orientation and frame instead of reproducing table.
March-of-progress silhouette suggests a ladder culminating in humans. Exclude that decorative image; use branching ancestry or allele-frequency change as appropriate.

sourceArtworkReuse: No blanket reuse clearance. Original figures preferred; any retained authentic image needs an individual provenance, use-scope and caption record.
